title: fix(gpt-oss): avoid duplicate MoE reduction with DP attention
body:
<!-- PR title: [Fix] Avoid duplicate GPT-OSS MoE reduction with DP attention -->
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #37187.

Enabling DP attention for GPT-OSS-120B with TP4/DP4/EP4 caused severe output corruption:

| Configuration | GSM8K first 128 | MMLU fixed 128 subset |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DP attention disabled | 124/128 | 110/128 |
| DP attention enabled | 0/128 | 4/128 |

Affected responses contained repeated Harmony channel markers, empty final
answers, and generations that frequently reached the 8192-token limit.

### Root cause

With MoE A2A disabled and `TP == attention DP == EP`, every TP rank initially
produces an expert partial `m_i`.

`GptOssSparseMoeBlock.forward_normal()` first performed a TP all-reduce, so
every rank held:

```text
s = m0 + m1 + ... + m(TP-1)
```

DP-attention postprocessing then called `reduce_scatterv` over the same TP
group. Since reduce-scatter also sums its inputs, it combined TP replicated
copies of `s`, producing approximately:

```text
TP * s
```

On TP4, the MoE output was therefore scaled by approximately 4x.

The residual branch was not scaled, so the following residual addition and
normalization could not cancel this error.

### Layer-level evidence

Using the same 80-token input on GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4 with TP4/EP4:

| First-layer boundary | DPA compared with healthy TP reference |
| --- | ---: |
| Input IDs, positions, embeddings, attention-norm input | Exact match |
| Reconstructed Q/K/V and attention-kernel output | Exact match |
| O-projection output | Relative L2 0.002145 |
| MoE input | Relative L2 0.003450 |
| MoE output RMS | 0.803564 -> 3.216738 |
| MoE output after multiplying DPA by 0.25 | Relative L2 0.021860 |
| Next attention-norm input | Relative L2 0.491051 |

The fitted DPA correction factor was `0.249747`, consistent with a duplicate
reduction on TP4.

## Modifications

- Make GPT-OSS use the centralized
  `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(is_tp_path=True)` ownership predicate.
- When DP-attention postprocessing owns the reduction, pass the original expert
  partials directly to `reduce_scatterv`.
- Preserve the existing model-side all-reduce for configurations where no
  downstream component owns the reduction.
- Add CPU regression tests covering:
  - TP4/DP4/EP4 with DPA: skip the model-side all-reduce
  - plain TP: preserve the all-reduce
  - fused MLP all-reduce: preserve the existing skip behavior
  - partial attention DP (`TP != attention DP`), including TP4/DP2/EP4:
    preserve all-reduce + scatter

This does not divide the output by TP size and does not modify the
reduce-scatter implementation.

### Scope and Limitations

This PR changes only GPT-OSS post-experts collective ownership. It does not
modify:

- attention or MoE kernels
- quantization
- KV-cache management
- parsers
- CUDA Graph
- overlap scheduling
- chunking

The GPU validation does not cover dynamic DWDP, other TP/DP/EP sizes, full
benchmark datasets, long-context retrieval, or post-fix throughput.

### Related Work

#33135 contains the same centralized GPT-OSS guard as part of a broader draft
FlashInfer A2A/routed-MoE change. This PR isolates the correctness fix and adds
the DP-attention reproduction, layer-level diagnosis, accuracy validation, and
focused regression coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation environment:

- Official `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18`
- `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, MXFP4 weights with BF16 activations
- 4x NVIDIA GB200
- TP4/DP4/EP4
- `trtllm_mha` attention
- `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE runner
- MoE A2A backend `none`

### Exact same-configuration smoke test

The launch parameters and effective chunk size were unchanged; the only
inference-code change was the post-experts reduction guard.

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Basic questions | 1/4 | 4/4 |
| Tool-call structure | Not run after failed smoke | Passed |

### Fixed-prompt accuracy

| Configuration | Effective chunk/rank | GSM8K first 128 | MMLU fixed 128 subset |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DPA disabled reference | 16384 | 124/128 | 110/128 |
| DPA enabled, original code | 16384 | 0/128 | 4/128 |
| DPA enabled, fixed | 16384 | 121/128 | 110/128 |

All 256 responses from the fixed run had:

- zero empty final answers
- zero 8192-token truncations
- zero API errors
- zero retry errors

The previous accuracy references used an effective chunk size of 16384,
whereas the fixed accuracy run used 4096. Therefore, the strict
same-configuration before/after comparison is the four-question smoke test.
The 256-question run demonstrates recovery to the healthy reference range,
not bitwise equivalence.

The subsets were:

- GSM8K: first 128 test questions with five-shot train examples
- MMLU: 100 `abstract_algebra` and 28 `anatomy` questions

They are diagnostic fixed subsets, not full benchmark scores.

### Unit tests and checks

- New GPT-OSS collective-guard CPU tests: 5/5 passed
- Related runtime-context helper tests: 2/2 passed
- `git diff --check`
- `py_compile`
- Black formatting check
- isort check
- PR Ruff rules
- registered-test CI validation

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No post-fix performance benchmark was run.

The change removes a redundant TP all-reduce from the affected path, but this
PR makes no performance claim. Previous throughput measurements were collected
before the correctness fix and are not used as post-fix performance evidence.
